title: chaos-errorpath: missing config exits rc=0 with fail-closed JSON — no usage/error surface, exit code lies to callers
reasoning: QA foreman cycle 2026-10-02 — fresh-system battery on dedi-2 (chaos-errorpath cell, agent cca2210e). With no config/env on a clean machine, guardd exits rc=0 printing {"decision":"block","risk_level":"medium","route":"quarantine","reason":"guard_error (fail-closed): no openrouter api key available",...}. The fail-closed DECISION is correct design, but the PROCESS exit code is 0 — shell/CI callers keying on rc (the standard errorpath contract: clean usage = rc!=0) see success. A wrapper that only checks rc, or that greps stderr for errors, treats a broken (keyless) deployment as healthy; the failure is only visible if the caller parses the JSON body's decision field. rc=0 is reasonable for a SERVING guard (decision block is the product), but the battery grades the CLI errorpath and the exit code does not distinguish 'classified' from 'config broken'.

title: P4 — Contract advertises decision value `sanitize` but no code path ever produces it; docs and code disagree on the value space
reasoning: Docs audit tick guard-docs-2026-10-02-05-18-54 @ HEAD ad22987, contract-vs-implementation diff. README.md:44 documents the decision space as 'allow | block | sanitize'; docs/ADOPTION.md:35 claims parity with crier on 'allow|block|sanitize'; guard.go:36 defines DecisionSanitize. The repo's own release recipe reproduces the flaw: `make release` snapshotted at this pin emits a binary whose `go version -m` reports go1.26.9. The fix is proven reachable, not assumed - go1.26.11 is published on go.dev/dl and the identical scan under GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.11 returns rc=0 'No vulnerabilities found'. The pin surface is split: go.mod carries the only explicit version, README.md:12 advertises it, and both workflows use the floating go-version: '1.26' which resolves to the latest patch, so nothing in the repo forces a patched floor. Publishing another tag from a pin that provably builds the vulnerable stdlib would republish the advisories under a newer version number. Classified not-proven-shipped: the v0.1.0 release run's resolved Go patch could not be recovered (gh run view 37054260017 --log returned no body).
